title: CSU Rams give up season-high points, yards in loss to Texas State
text:
The Bobcats scored on seven straight possessions in the first half, the first four of which came before the Rams got on the scoreboard.
Trinity AudioUnder new defensive play caller Kenny McClendon, the Colorado State defense forced Texas State to punt on its first possession Thursday night in San Marcos.
The Bobcats then scored on seven straight possessions in the first half, the first four of which came before the Rams got on the scoreboard. The loss was the fourth in a row for CSU after the Rams won their first two games. CSU also fell to 0-2 in Pac-12 play.
McClendon took over the Rams’ defense after former defensive coordinator Tyson Summers left the field during CSU’s game against Oregon State on Oct. 3 and was let go after the contest. However, CSU gave up more than 55 points and 500 yards for the third week in a row. The 66 points and 716 yards the defense allowed were season-highs. Both teams faced fourth-and-1 on their opening drives, and both chose to punt.
Texas State scored its first touchdown of the game on its second possession, and the Rams couldn’t stop the Bobcats the rest of the half. After their defense gave up four touchdowns in the first 18 minutes and 10 seconds of the game, the Rams offense began to chip away at the Bobcats’ lead. The Rams recovered a fumble on a Texas State punt return and needed two plays to score.
Durell Robinson ran it in from 15 yards out to cut the Bobcats advantage to 28-7. After Texas State went ahead 35-7, CSU quarterback K’saan Farrar found Nader Chirchi for a 21-yard touchdown to make it 35-14. The Bobcats answered again to go up 42-14, but the Rams responded with a 1-yard run by Robinson to cut the Texas State lead to 42-21 with 26 seconds remaining in the first half.
It turned out to be enough time for Texas State to kick a 23-yard field goal and take a 45-21 lead into halftime. CSU opened the second half with a 37-yard touchdown pass from Farrar to Terrence Smith that cut the Texas State lead to 45-27 after a failed two-point conversion attempt, but that would be as close as the Rams would get.
Texas State scored three more times in the third quarter, and neither team scored in the game’s final 15 minutes. Of the Bobcats’ 716 yards of offense, they rushed for 496. Torrance Burgess rushed for 224 yards and four touchdowns while quarterback Brad Jackson ran for 181 yards and three touchdowns. Jackson also passed for 213 yards and a touchdown.
For CSU, Farrar passed for 282 yards and two touchdowns. Jackson Harper caught five passes for 91 yards and the Rams collectively rushed for 148 yards and two TDs, both by Robinson.
